title: Self-Data Distillation for Recovering Quality in Pruned Large Language Models
problem: Structured depth pruning of LLMs removes decoder blocks and reduces compute, but post-pruning SFT causes catastrophic forgetting by shifting the data distribution away from the original model's knowledge.
motivation: One-shot pruning removes up to 6 decoder layers from a 32-layer model, significantly degrading accuracy. Vanilla SFT on the original fine-tuning dataset exacerbates forgetting because the responses no longer reflect the unpruned model's knowledge. A method is needed to recover quality while preserving the efficiency gains of pruning.
method: The method identifies redundant layers by measuring angular cosine distance (how similar the outputs from adjacent layers are in their directional orientation) — the most similar outputs mark the best layers to remove. The original unpruned model regenerates the training dataset by creating high-quality responses that preserve semantic meaning, while selectively keeping original responses for prompts where the pruned model already performs well. The pruned model and the version trained on these regenerated responses are merged using SLERP merging (spherical linear interpolation, which blends model weights along the shortest path), and the pruned model can also function as a draft generator in speculative decoding paired with the full model as verifier.
key_novelty: Using the unpruned model to regenerate a semantically-aligned fine-tuning dataset prevents catastrophic forgetting in depth-pruned models, while also enabling SLERP model merging (a method to blend two model versions) and speculative decoding.
contributions: Angular cosine distance metric for depth-wise block pruning candidate identification
Self-data distillation: unpruned model rewrites fine-tuning responses to prevent catastrophic forgetting
Conditional selection to preserve original responses where pruned model is already adequate
SLERP model merging for additional quality recovery
Speculative decoding application: pruned model as draft (+1.70 average accepted length at block size 10)
91.24% accuracy retention at block size 6 vs 81.66% for standard SFT on Llama3.1-8B
hardware_target: GPU inference (A100-class); edge deployment of pruned models
limitations: Self-data distillation requires running inference on the full unpruned model, incurring generation cost
Angular cosine metric may not capture all relevant structural information for pruning
Evaluated primarily on Llama3.1-8B and Mistral-7B; larger models may behave differently
